$comment: Kodukeel API v1 (ADR-029). Generated by `npm run api:schema` from lib/api/contract.ts and lib/api/draft.ts; do not edit. A route marked draft may still change. A response may gain fields within v1, so a client ignores fields it does not know.

body.description: Every refusal from a v1 route, whatever its status.

GET /api/v1/meta.summary: The API version, the oldest native build still answered, what is switched off, the speech model's pins and how to sign in.

response.description: What this installation is, for a native app before it signs in. Nothing about any person.

GET /api/v1/me.summary: Who the token belongs to, and the language they read the app in.

GET /api/v1/review.summary: Today's review sitting, as the web's review session receives it.

items.description: One run of a sentence, with the dictionary entry it was vouched as, if any.

intro.description: What to show the first time this word is met; null on a card already seen.

anyOf.description: A meaning as the learner's language leads it; the English is never dropped while an equivalent leads.

items.description: A meaning as the learner's language leads it; the English is never dropped while an equivalent leads.

scheduling.description: A card's scheduling, as a grade leaves it and as undo puts it back.

items.description: One card of a review sitting, as the web's review session receives it.

nextDue.description: When the next card comes back, on an empty sitting alone; the line is in the learner's language.

waitingOnCourse.description: Whether unseen cards are held back until the course reaches them.

response.description: Today's review sitting: due cards, then a capped trickle of new ones, held to what the course has taught.

POST /api/v1/grades.summary: One grade or a batch, idempotent by id, as the offline outbox replays them.

id.description: The id the device chose for this answer, before it asked. Sending it twice records it once.

reviewedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds on the device, clamped by the server to the last thirty days and to never after it heard.

slot.description: What the round asked about, where narrower than the card; checked against a closed list.

reachedSlot.description: The form that came back instead, where the round could name one.

spoken.description: True only where the answer marked is what the recognizer heard, word for word.

settled.description: Every id the client may now drop: recorded now, recorded before, or never recordable.

anyOf.description: A card's scheduling, as a grade leaves it and as undo puts it back.

scheduling.description: What this request left the card at, or null where it wrote nothing now.

results.description: One entry per grade written by this request, in the order they were applied.

POST /api/v1/grades/undo.summary: A card's scheduling put back; the review log is untouched.

previous.description: The scheduling the card had before the grade being taken back, as the grade's own answer gave it.

GET /api/v1/today.summary: Whether today is a lesson, a check, the web or nothing planned.

finished.description: True where today's lesson is already done; the next one waits for tomorrow.

final.description: Whether this is the check on the whole of the level.

passed.description: Whether the part after it is open; false until the check is passed.

href.description: The path of today on the web, under the deployment's own address.

response.description: Whether today is a lesson, a check, the web or nothing planned.

GET /api/v1/lessons/{id}.summary: One lesson, as the web's lesson screen receives it, with its English in the learner's language.

cast.description: Who speaks, by name, and the voice each is read in.

sounds.description: Recordings by id, as `GET /api/v1/recordings` names them.

examples.description: Lines of the conversation, by index.

lesson.description: One lesson as the web's lesson screen receives it. Two conventions run through its English, and a native screen draws them as the web's `Braced` does: Estonian inside an English sentence is written in braces, `{mina}`, and is marked as Estonian; a form's name in square brackets, `[osastav] (3rd form)`, is Estonian too and is not a word the lesson teaches. A capital I in a form's English hint is set in a face where it cannot be read as a lower-case l. The stand-in name Tom in a model answer is replaced by the learner's own `name` after translating. The Estonian was written for a beginner and read by a native speaker; a client draws it as it stands and never joins, respells or builds a line.

accept.description: Every spelling that counts, the asked one first.

items.description: One question, built on the server; the client never decides what a learner is asked.

accept.description: Every spelling that counts, the asked one first.

items.description: One question, built on the server; the client never decides what a learner is asked.

next.description: The next lesson in the same level, or null at its end.

scene.description: The lesson's own conversation, a scene id, where it has one.

name.description: The learner's own first name, for a model answer about them.

due.description: Cards due in the learner's reviews now.

check.description: The check that closes this lesson's part, where this is its last lesson.

nativePart.description: The one part of the conversation the native speaker recorded whole, which a phone plays in his voice by `GET /api/v1/recordings`; every other part keeps the cast's synthetic voice, as on the web (N-6).

translations.description: The lesson's own English in the learner's language, keyed by the English it replaces, for every line a translation exists for; empty in English. The Estonian is never in it and never changes.

response.description: One lesson, as the web's lesson screen receives it.

POST /api/v1/lessons/{id}/finish.summary: A finished lesson: today ticked where it is today's, and its words in the deck.

recorded.description: Whether today's evening was ticked; false for a lesson ahead of today, which records nothing.

GET /api/v1/checks/{id}.summary: One attempt's paper at a part's check.

items.description: The attempt's questions as the web's check screen receives them, the right answers included, which the web uses for feedback too; the mark is the server's.

accept.description: Every spelling that counts, the asked one first.

items.description: One question, built on the server; the client never decides what a learner is asked.

needed.description: How many marks a pass takes.

response.description: One attempt's paper at a part's check.

POST /api/v1/checks/{id}.summary: An attempt marked on the server, and a pass recorded.

attempt.description: The attempt the paper was fetched for; the server builds that paper again to mark it.

responses.description: What was picked or typed for each question, in order; null where nothing was.

response.description: The attempt marked on the server. A right answer is one point and a nearly half.

GET /api/v1/dictionary.summary: A dictionary search, the forms list and Ekilex asked as the web's dictionary asks them.

q.description: What was typed: a headword, an inflected form, or English.

matchedAs.description: Set where the query was an inflected form rather than the headword, the form named the way a class names it.

hits.description: The entries found, the likeliest first; `GET /api/v1/words/{id}` opens one.

knownAs.description: Where nothing matched directly, the headwords the spelling typed is a form of, the likeliest first.

fetched.description: Whether the dictionary asked Ekilex live to answer this search.

response.description: A dictionary search, as the web's dictionary page runs it.

GET /api/v1/words/{id}.summary: One dictionary entry, as the web's entry screen reads it.

translationRu.description: The Institute's own Russian, where Ekilex recorded one; never a model's.

translationUk.description: The Institute's own Ukrainian, where Ekilex recorded one; never a model's.

ekilexWordId.description: The Ekilex word this entry was read from, or null where Ekilex supplied none of it. Where it is set, the entry carries the credit CC BY 4.0 asks for, as the web draws it: forms and example sentences from Ekilex (https://ekilex.ee), by the Institute of the Estonian Language, under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/), and any form shown as worked out was derived from what Ekilex stores.

et.description: The Estonian sentence, exactly as recorded.

en.description: Its English, where the dictionary holds one.

enRefused.description: A reviewer read the English and said it was wrong; none is offered.

examples.description: Recorded sentences, the one a beginner reads most easily first. A refused sentence never arrives.

forms.description: The forms the dictionary stores; the rest are worked out on the device from these, as the web does.

response.description: One dictionary entry, as the web's entry screen reads it. Nothing in it was written by a model.

POST /api/v1/deck.summary: A word kept, starred or put aside.

types.description: Which cards to build; a word builds only the ones it can support. The three the dictionary ticks by default.

context.description: Where the word was when it was put aside, for the reading the operator sees.

added.description: Cards built by a keep; 0 otherwise, and 0 where the word was already in the deck.

starred.description: Whether the word is starred now, after a star or an unstar; null otherwise.

note.description: The English sentence saying how long the word is away.

aside.description: How long a word put aside is away for; null otherwise. Nothing is graded.

response.description: A word kept, starred, put aside or brought back.

DELETE /api/v1/deck.summary: A star taken off, or a word put aside brought back.

action.description: `star` takes the star off; `aside` brings a word put aside back.

added.description: Cards built by a keep; 0 otherwise, and 0 where the word was already in the deck.

starred.description: Whether the word is starred now, after a star or an unstar; null otherwise.

note.description: The English sentence saying how long the word is away.

aside.description: How long a word put aside is away for; null otherwise. Nothing is graded.

response.description: A word kept, starred, put aside or brought back.

POST /api/v1/tts.summary: A clip read aloud, from the same store and under the same allowance as the web's.

text.description: What to read aloud, finished into a sentence on the server.

voice.description: One of the voices Settings offers; any other value is the deployment's own.

transient.description: A read-back of what the recognizer heard: never cached, never stored, and refused while speaking is switched off.

POST /api/v1/speech/forms.summary: Which heard words are Estonian spellings.

words.description: The words heard, and nothing else; at most sixty are asked, each up to forty letters.

known.description: Those of `asked` that are Estonian spellings.

asked.description: The words asked about, lowercased and deduplicated.

response.description: Which words just heard are Estonian spellings at all.

GET /api/v1/recordings.summary: The native speaker's clips and the spelling each answers for.

text.description: What is said, as it is written; for a letter, the letter.

src.description: Where the clip is served, under this site.

key.description: The spelling a speaker button finds this clip by, folded as `utteranceKey` folds it, or null where the clip is played by id alone: a sound, a letter's name, and a spelling that hides two words.

slow.description: A take said slowly on purpose; a speaker asked to play slowly takes it before the take at speed.

atOwnSpeed.description: Played at the speed it was said: by id always, and a slow take asked for slowly. Found by `key` at the learner's everyday pace, the player slows it as it slows a synthetic clip.

response.description: The native speaker's recordings, and which spelling each one answers for.

spoken.description: Counts only, never the words heard. `unseen` is true only where the line answered was hidden on screen.

POST /api/v1/scenes/{runId}/help.summary: Help asked for in a conversation.

POST /api/v1/chat.summary: Today's chat begun, where a model is configured.

request.description: Draft: every field optional, each validated as its Settings action validates it.

response.description: The backup the web's export downloads.
